title: Performance Optimization
description: Learn to profile, memoize, and tune Redux applications to avoid unnecessary re-renders and expensive computations.

data.text: Redux itself is fast, but **referential equality** issues in selectors and components are the #1 cause of slow Redux apps. Optimizing Redux means making sure components only re-render when their slice of state actually changes.

data.title: Profile first
data.text: Don't optimize blindly. Use the React DevTools Profiler to record a slow interaction and see which components re-render and why.
`useSelector` uses `===` by default. If your selector returns a **new array or object every time** — even with the same contents — every component subscribed to it will re-render on every dispatch.

data.title: Bad selector
data.content: Returns a fresh array on every call
data.code:
export const selectActiveUsers = (state) =>
  state.users.filter((u) => u.active); // new array each time!

data.text: `createSelector` (from Redux Toolkit / Reselect) **caches** its result. It only recomputes when its input selectors return new values.

data.title: Memoized selector
data.content: Recomputes only when todos or filter change

data.caption: Memoized selectors only recompute when their inputs actually change.

data.title: Common Redux optimizations
rows: New function references on each render
Distinct domains with separate update rates

cards.title: React.memo
cards.description: HOC that skips re-render if props are shallow-equal.
cons: Doesn't help with internal state or hooks
Useless if you pass new object/function props

cards.title: useMemo
cards.description: Hook that returns a cached value across renders.
cons: Cache invalidates on every dep change

cards.title: createSelector
cons: Must be called outside render (module scope)

data.text: If a selector returns a primitive array you mutate elsewhere, pass a custom equality function to `useSelector`.

data.title: Custom equality
data.content: Avoid re-render when array contents are the same

data.text: Storing lists of objects as arrays causes expensive re-renders when any item updates. **Normalize** them into `{ ids: [], entities: {} }` so updates to one item don't change references for the whole list.

data.title: createEntityAdapter

terms.definition: Caching the result of a function based on its inputs.
Two values are equal because they are the same object reference (`===`).
Comparing the top-level keys of an object or items of an array with `===`.
Storing entities in an `entities` lookup keyed by id so individual updates don't ripple.

data.title: Watch for over-memoization
data.text: Memoization is not free. Each `createSelector` keeps its previous inputs in memory. Only memoize expensive or unstable derivations.

data.title: Profile and fix a slow TodoList
data.description:
1. Open React DevTools Profiler and record a click on a single todo checkbox.
2. Notice that every TodoItem re-renders even though only one changed.
3. Add `createSelector` for `selectFilteredTodos`.
4. Wrap `TodoItem` in `React.memo`.
5. Verify with Profiler that only the changed item re-renders.
steps: Pass primitive props to memoized children, not freshly-built objects.
Entity adapters can replace `todos` arrays with `entities` lookup for big wins.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Profile before optimizing — use React DevTools Profiler
Use `shallowEqual` or `React.memo` for components subscribed to unstable shapes
Memoization costs memory — only use it where it pays off
data.takeaway: Memoization and normalization prevent unnecessary re-renders.
